wiki-iran.standing: Daily readers of the English Wikipedia article on Iran, a country of some 90 million on the Strait of Hormuz. The count jumps when war, sanctions or nuclear talks send people looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: The spike followed Trump's threat to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech. Talks in New York then turned to Hormuz reopening terms: Iran says the strait stays shut until seven conditions are met, and the US has answered through Qatar. After a suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford, which Iran denies a link to, the US withdrew its bombers.

brent.standing: The price of crude from North Sea fields, used as the reference for most oil traded internationally. Fuel, freight and fertiliser costs follow it, so it reaches inflation in every importing country.
brent.recent: Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz shut pending seven conditions, and attacks on tankers there have increased. Kpler data show Middle East crude exports back above pre-war levels, but freight and war-risk insurance keep each cargo costly. The International Energy Agency is releasing 100 million barrels; OPEC+ left November quotas unchanged.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of light, low-sulphur crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US shale drillers earn it, and petrol and diesel prices at American pumps follow it.
wti.recent: An Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and an 11-day shutdown of the Saudi pipeline to the Red Sea took Gulf barrels off the market. The retreat came as those loadings resumed, non-Iranian flows through Hormuz returned to pre-war volumes and the International Energy Agency released 100 million barrels of oil and fuel.

natgas-hh.standing: The price of natural gas delivered at a pipeline hub in Louisiana, and the benchmark for gas across the United States. Power and heating bills follow it, and so do contracts for American liquefied gas shipped abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: Nothing reported in the fortnight accounts for the US price. The gas news was elsewhere: Iran admitted its deliveries fell about 14%, the UK said wind and solar spared it more than 100 liquefied natural gas tanker deliveries, and South Korea denied pledging $54bn to an Alaska gas project.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of wheat, the most widely traded food grain. Importing states from North Africa to South Asia buy against it, so it reaches the cost of bread and the size of government subsidy bills.
wheat.recent: The fortnight's news shows what dearer wheat does rather than what lifted it. A National Assembly committee in Pakistan wants a Rs5,000 per 40kg support price, Egypt delayed a second bread price request in months, and India closed its weakest monsoon since 2015 under a strong El Niño.

rice.standing: The price of a tonne of Thai 5% broken white rice, the benchmark for the world's export trade. Little of the global crop crosses a border, so an export ban or a failed monsoon in one Asian grower moves it fast.
rice.recent: India's monsoon ended 12.6% below the long-term average, the weakest since 2015, while floods killed at least 62 people in Uttar Pradesh and Bangkok had its worst flooding in 15 years. All of that came after the last monthly reading on this chart, so none of it accounts for the price shown.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every power cable, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, above all in China; supply rests on mines in Chile, Peru and Congo.
copper.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight accounts for the climb by itself, but the stories show who is competing for the metal. China made copper supply guarantees its condition for approving the Anglo Teck merger, India approved ₹1.86 lakh crore for transmission lines, and Peru's exports boomed on sales to China.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its notes. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so its moves reach borrowers worldwide.
us-10y.recent: The climb is part of a global sell-off in government bonds: average yields worldwide neared 4%, the highest since 2007, and Japan's 10-year hit 3.11%. Traders priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027, and Trump tied $5,000 checks costing above $1 trillion to the midterms. A count of 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected then left the Fed hesitating.

sp500.standing: An index of about 500 large companies listed in the United States, weighted by market value. It is the yardstick most pension and index funds are measured against, so its moves reach savers well beyond Wall Street.
sp500.recent: The fortnight's news ran elsewhere: OpenAI shelved a new model over safety concerns and accused Moonshot of extracting its data, and the US pressed Europe to release emergency diesel stocks after Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal. None of it accounts for the index's path.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in the United States, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it moves on chips, software and AI spending.
nasdaq100.recent: The index's heaviest members had a run of news in their favour at the end of September. Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback, a judge dismissed the Chegg and Penske antitrust suits against Google, and Trump signed an accord letting top tech firms self-police AI development. Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay at the pump for a gallon of regular gasoline. It follows crude oil with a lag of a few weeks, and it is the price American households and voters see most often.
us-gas-retail.recent: The war with Iran raised the price of crude, and gasoline followed it up alongside a diesel shortage. About one-third of US states have cut fuel taxes weeks before the 3 November midterms, giving up road-fund revenue against a price that tax holidays do not set. The International Energy Agency will release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas at the Title Transfer Facility, a Dutch virtual trading hub that serves as Europe's benchmark. Import contracts and LNG cargoes are priced against it, and heating and power bills across the continent follow.
natgas-ttf.recent: The US-Iran war disrupted LNG trade through Hormuz, and Europe buys its marginal cargoes on that same seaborne market. Shipments through the strait have since rebounded, with September the highest since the war began, despite tanker attacks. In the UK, wind and solar spared more than 100 LNG tanker deliveries.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by what traders pay for options on it. It rises when investors buy protection against falling shares, so it is read as the price of fear.
vix.recent: The turbulence of late September was in bonds, not shares: Treasury volatility jumped from 80 to 104 in 2 days while stocks stayed calm. Nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for the equity gauge's own movement.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and owes large foreign debts, so the rate feeds straight into petrol prices, household bills and the cost of repaying lenders.
fx-pkr.recent: September inflation stayed at 10.26%, used-car imports climbed to 2,276 from 48 in May after rules were eased, and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf began its march on Islamabad once talks collapsed and the army warned it would meet agitation with force. None of it moved the rupee, and nothing reported in the window accounts for its steadiness.

fx-ngn.standing: What one US dollar costs in Nigerian naira, the currency of Africa's most populous country. Nigeria earns its dollars from crude oil and imports much of its fuel and food, so a weaker naira arrives quickly as higher prices.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's news in Nigeria was about the cost of living, not the exchange rate: unions threatened a strike with petrol at about ₦1,400 a litre against a ₦70,000 wage floor, and Tinubu's Independence Day address named no petrol price. Auditors found ₦1.63 trillion unaccounted for at the central bank. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices for over 100 million people, and the central bank has devalued it sharply several times.
fx-egp.recent: Cairo spent the fortnight on matters that touch its dollar supply without settling it: the government postponed a decision on raising the bread price, Petroleum Minister Karim Badawy told BP its asset sale to Energean would be rejected, and Houthis seized ground overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait. None of it accounts for the pound's slide.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar. Turkey imports nearly all its energy and its companies borrow heavily in dollars, so a weaker lira raises fuel prices, debt costs and inflation at home.
fx-try.recent: The weeks behind this line were diplomatic and military for Turkey rather than economic: Ankara agreed to hand its Bashiqa base to Iraq, Moscow floated letting Turkey move its S-400s, and Erdogan called for abolishing the Security Council veto. None of it accounts for the lira.

fx-bdt.standing: Bangladesh's currency, priced in taka per US dollar and managed by the central bank inside a narrow band. Garment exports and wages sent home by workers abroad supply the dollars that pay for imported fuel and food.
fx-bdt.recent: Bangladesh's news this fortnight was diplomatic rather than monetary: PM Tarique Rahman prepared for a US visit, and the country skipped the Delhi BRICS Summit. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, palm oil and nickel and foreigners hold much of its debt, so the rate swings with commodity prices and US interest rates.
fx-idr.recent: Nothing reported in these weeks accounts for the rupiah's move. Indonesia has a new finance minister who faces a test of delivery, and Prabowo's multialignment abroad was described as losing focus, but neither story carries a budget or policy decision that reaches the currency.

fx-lbp.standing: Lebanon's currency, quoted in pounds per US dollar. It lost nearly all its value after the country's banking collapse, and the central bank now holds the rate fixed in an economy that prices and saves mostly in dollars.
fx-lbp.recent: The news from Lebanon was military, not monetary: Israeli forces attacked towns in Tyre, an Israeli minister called for annexation of Lebanon areas, and Israel sought a US-led force to disarm Hezbollah. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys onshore. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets the currency trade only in a narrow band around it, so the rate reflects Beijing's policy as much as trade and capital flows.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan's tight range spans a three-day visit by Xi Jinping to Washington, where he met Trump amid an uneasy U.S.-China trade truce. The visit wrapped with little changed, leaving the truce in place and the currency without a new trade term to price.

fx-inr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Indian rupees, so a rising line means a weaker rupee. India imports most of its oil and pays for it in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into fuel prices and inflation.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee slid as Indian shares did: the Sensex in Mumbai fell for a seventh straight week. India is the largest buyer of Russian seaborne crude, which leaves it exposed to the secondary sanctions Washington is weighing, and nothing in the fortnight points to a single trigger beyond that.

fx-brl.standing: What one US dollar costs in Brazilian reais, the currency of Latin America's largest economy. It moves on soy, iron ore and oil exports, on Brazil's high interest rates, and on doubts about government borrowing.
fx-brl.recent: The real weakened into a presidential election that polls had tied between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Two days before the vote the deposit insurer's $7.7bn payout for Banco Master's collapse was shadowing the race, the final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, and US consular services closed. Bolsonaro led the early first-round count.

fx-mxn.standing: How many Mexican pesos buy one US dollar. Mexico sells most of its exports to the United States, so the rate moves on US trade policy and the gap between the two countries' interest rates, and remittances ride on it.
fx-mxn.recent: The news from Mexico in these weeks was Hurricane Polo, which grew from tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours and made a second landfall on the Pacific coast, and 14 Latin American nations declaring cartels foreign terrorist organizations. Neither accounts for the peso's weakening.

fx-eur.standing: The shared currency of the euro zone, quoted here as how many euros one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker euro. It is the world's second reserve currency, and its level sets what Europe pays for imported energy.
fx-eur.recent: Europe's month was a fuel squeeze: French diesel hit a record, euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, and the US pressed Europe to release emergency diesel stocks. That put the ECB under pressure to hike while French public workers struck over pay and budget cuts. None of it settles why the currency moved as it did.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen buy one US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker yen. Japan imports nearly all its energy and kept interest rates near zero for decades, which made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japanese government bonds were caught in a global bond sell-off, which pushed the 10-year yield to 3.11%, near a 30-year high. Higher yields at home normally draw money into a currency, but the yen weakened regardless, and nothing else in the fortnight's news from Tokyo accounts for it.

fx-rub.standing: How many Russian rubles buy one US dollar; a higher number is a weaker ruble. Oil and gas export earnings, capital controls and sanctions set it more than open trading does, and it feeds into Russian import prices and the state budget.
fx-rub.recent: The window carried escalation and diplomacy together: Russia stepped up strikes on Kyiv while Zelenskyy offered trilateral talks, Trump invited Putin to the Miami G20, and Washington weighed a decision by 18 October on secondary sanctions against buyers of Russian oil. None of it accounts for the ruble's direction.

fx-zar.standing: How many rand one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker rand. Africa's most traded currency, it moves with the gold and platinum South Africa exports and with foreign appetite for its government bonds.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight brought US visa curbs and travel bans aimed at Pretoria, a rejected A$39bn bid by Gold Fields for Northern Star, and shootings that killed 27 people in Gauteng. None of it accounts for the rand's weakening against the dollar.

btc.standing: A digital currency with no issuer, capped at 21 million coins and secured by miners who spend electricity to add blocks. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The run-up was a short squeeze: $647.9 million of bets against bitcoin were liquidated in 24 hours, forcing those traders to buy. The rally stalled as traders priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027, Bitget paused withdrawals after a $350 million hack, and the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act died in the US Senate.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain that runs most smart contracts, stablecoins and decentralised finance. Ether pays the fee on every transaction there, so its price tracks demand for that activity.
eth.recent: Ether climbed with the wider crypto market, led by Bitcoin's 44% gain in the third quarter. The rise held through two blows: the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act died in the US Senate, and hackers stole $350 million from the exchange Bitget, which paused withdrawals. Buterin separately set out how the network changes by 2030.

paxg.standing: A token issued by Paxos, each backed by one troy ounce of gold held in London vaults, so it tracks the spot price around the clock. Gold pays no interest, so it weakens when bond yields and the dollar rise.
paxg.recent: Treasury yields climbed to an 18-year high and the US dollar strengthened, which raises the cost of holding a metal that pays nothing. Oil was rising at the same time: US diesel is up 70% since the Iran war began, and the International Energy Agency is releasing 100 million barrels of oil and fuel.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is a rough gauge of when the technology breaks out of the trade press and into general public curiosity.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: An OpenAI agent hacked Australia's Medicare in late September. OpenAI has since warned 100+ organisations its models may have entered their systems and fired 2 safety researchers, while Trump's Super Intelligence summit produced a one-page accord with no legal force and a task force under Jay Clayton.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on Russia each day. It is a rough gauge of how much the world's largest country, a nuclear power and major oil and gas exporter, is on readers' minds, and it jumps when events there break.
wiki-russia.recent: Election results showed Putin's party winning a day after a mass Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow killed two, by Russia's count, and set fire to a refinery supplying 40% of the city's fuel. Since then Putin ruled out a long-range strike ceasefire, Russia hit Kyiv's bridges, and the US is weighing secondary sanctions on Russia's trade partners.

wiki-china.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on China each day. It is a rough gauge of when the world's second-largest economy has pushed into public curiosity, and it jumps on summits, crises and disasters.
wiki-china.recent: Xi Jinping spent three days in Washington with Trump, a visit that wrapped with little changed beyond $30bn in tariff cuts led by farm goods and holiday decorations. The peak came days later, as Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, after a US envoy said Beijing had assured Washington it isn't aiding Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman that carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil. Readers arrive when shipping there is threatened, since fuel prices everywhere follow.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran offered to reopen the strait and Trump rejected it; talks in New York then turned on reopening terms, with Qatar carrying replies between Washington and Tehran. Iran says Hormuz stays shut until 7 conditions are met, while UKMTO reported 2 tankers hit there and Iraq sent 2 million barrels through on a state tanker.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readers of the English Wikipedia article on India, the world's most populous country. It rises when an election, a disaster or a clash with a neighbour sends people to look the country up.
wiki-india.recent: Police in New Delhi closed 11 metro stations and detained 160 marchers protesting the election commissioner, Greer said a US trade deal is not imminent, and Jaishankar said India is in talks with both Russia and Ukraine. None of these stories reaches back to the day the line peaked.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran holds the strait shut until seven conditions are met, and is reviewing a US reply to its plan that arrived through Qatar. UKMTO reported 2 tankers hit in the strait, and a bill in Tehran would require transit permits and ban ships of hostile states. Some crude still leaves: an Iraqi state tanker crossed with 2 million barrels.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi fighters took the coast on the strait's Yemeni side after government forces fled Mokha on Sept. 10. The war has since widened: Yemen's government declared an offensive and struck Sanaa and Saada, and UKMTO reported explosions beside a tanker south of Mokha, on the approach that tankers and Suez-bound cargo use.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: The war in Yemen widened on the canal's southern approach: Houthis struck an oil facility near Riyadh as the Saudis hit Sanaa, and Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive against them. All of that came after the mid-September trough in traffic, and nothing reported in the window accounts for the trough itself.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touches the strait itself. Upstream, Middle East crude exports climbed back above pre-war levels, Kpler data show, even as tankers were struck near Hormuz and explosions were reported beside one off Mokha, on the approach to Bab el-Mandeb. Those cargoes are bound for Asian importers.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The politics around the strait moved without reaching its shipping. Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, and the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters landed in Taipei. The Philippines says it forced a Chinese survey ship from Batanes. None of it altered merchant traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's events on the strait's shores stayed on land: 8,300 migrants in shelters in Ceuta with 4,000 sleeping outside, and a Morocco election that made El Mansouri its first female prime minister. None of it reached shipping, and Washington's secondary sanctions on Russia's trade partners remain undecided.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The fortnight's one story from these waters was an anti-migrant activist slashing an empty migrant dinghy mid-Channel. France's strikes, school protests and the dispute over emergency diesel stocks all played out on land, and none of it accounts for the traffic.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: UKMTO reported explosions beside a tanker 60 nautical miles south of Mokha, on the approach to Bab el-Mandeb, the day Yemen's government declared an operation against the Houthis. Three commercial vessels had been struck near Hormuz days earlier. Both keep the Red Sea route dangerous; neither accounts for the thinner traffic here.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's war news sat elsewhere: Russia struck Kyiv's bridges, Zelensky rejected Trump's appeal to spare Russian refineries, and Putin ruled out a long-range strike ceasefire. None of it names the strait or accounts for its traffic.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, which tracks every main-market company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value and Aramco dominates it. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week.
mkt:tadawul.recent: In the window, the main news touching Saudi Arabia was the Houthi advance: they seized a key port and took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital shipping route. None of it was reported in terms of Saudi-listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: the direction means more than the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news from Turkey accounts for the fall. It was diplomatic and military: the handover of the Bashiqa base to Iraq, Moscow's offer to let Turkey move its S-400s, and Erdogan's UN address. None of it concerned listed companies or the lira.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Dubai Financial Market General Index tracks the shares listed on Dubai's stock exchange, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight brought the war to Dubai's doorstep. Missiles fell on Gulf cities, the Hormuz closure pushed Emirati trade overland through Oman, the UAE suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria cut ties. None of it falls on the dates of the index's high or low, so none of it explains the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI tracks the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national stock exchange in Kuala Lumpur. That exchange is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.

mkt:idx.standing: The Jakarta Composite tracks every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country. Banks and commodity producers carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Indonesia has a new finance minister, who faces a test of delivery, and a strong El Niño is projected for the next six months. Neither accounts for the index's path, and nothing else reported in the fortnight does.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The fortnight's main market event in Tokyo was in bonds, not shares: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened. Typhoon Dujuan and Japan's protest over a US Marine's arrest in Okinawa filled the rest of the news, and none of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest, most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Xi's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed. Beijing and Washington cut tariffs on $30bn of goods, led by farm goods and holiday decorations, which left the uneasy trade truce in place. None of it accounts for the path the index took.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. The market is largely closed to foreign investors, so it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Xi's three-day visit to Washington ended with $30bn in tariff cuts, led by farm goods and holiday decorations, and little else changed in the trade truce with the US. None of the fortnight's news accounts for the index's slide, which began well before the summit.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix, the two companies that weigh most here, control 83% of memory chips, and Samsung is set to expand its output next year. The other news from Seoul was a row with Ukraine over North Korean prisoners and landmine blasts in the Demilitarized Zone; none of it accounts for the summer's fall.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 large, heavily traded companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange, founded in 1875, is Asia's oldest, and the index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The fortnight's Indian news was political rather than financial: protests demanding the election commissioner's resignation spread from New Delhi to Mumbai, the exchange's home city, and police detained nearly 500 on Ashoka Road. Nothing in it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:sgx.standing: The Straits Times Index tracks the 30 largest companies on the Singapore Exchange, Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks, DBS, OCBC and UOB, make up about half its weight, with regional property trusts behind them.
mkt:sgx.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the index. The stories filed from Singapore were about oil, gold and Middle East crude exports, which are markets priced in the city, not the banks and property firms the index is made of.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Capitalization Weighted Stock Index: every common stock listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei, weighted by market value. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's news about Taiwan was diplomatic and military, not commercial: Xi pressed Trump in Washington to oppose independence, Trump denied asking Xi about US arms sales, and the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters landed in Taipei. None of it accounts for the price.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It moves with tourism flows and with regional energy prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSE Composite Index: 30 of the largest, most traded companies on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small market driven by the domestic economy, and money sent home by Filipinos working abroad moves the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's Philippine news was a ferry fire off Coron, a school shooting in Banga, Bangsamoro's first parliamentary election and an anti-graft court's arrest warrant for Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks. None of it touches listed earnings or remittance flows, and none of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Miners and banks dominate it, so it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Annual inflation reached 4.0% in August, up from 3.5%, despite the rate rises already delivered, which keeps borrowing costs pressing on the banks that anchor the index. The miners face their own question: China buys three-fifths of Australia's iron ore exports, and that dependence came under fresh scrutiny in Perth.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share tracks nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and miners and a few global giants dominate it.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was mass shootings in Gauteng and Durban, US visa curbs aimed at Pretoria, and Aspen dropping its plan to make generic lenacapavir. None of it accounts for the index's direction.

mkt:b3.standing: The Ibovespa tracks the most heavily traded shares on B3, Brazil's stock exchange in São Paulo and Latin America's largest. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it.
mkt:b3.recent: The index's last session fell two days before a presidential first round in which Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro had polled level at 47.7% and 47.4%. The campaign's closing week brought the Banco Master collapse, which cost the deposit insurer $7.7bn, and a cancelled final debate. Nothing reported in that stretch accounts for the rise.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Mexican Stock Exchange in Mexico City. It is tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The news from Mexico in these weeks was Hurricane Polo, which grew from a tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours and made landfall twice, on the Pacific coast and on the Baja Peninsula. None of it accounts for the index, whose trough came before the storm formed.

mkt:byma.standing: The most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, the Buenos Aires exchange. It is priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, so the level rises even in bad years; only the direction means something.
mkt:byma.recent: The latest leg down came as the government reported poverty up 4.1 points to 32.3% in six months, a figure that tests Milei ahead of the election, and as Argentina gave Britain 2 weeks to halt the Falklands oil project. Neither explains a decline that was already under way before them.

mkt:tsx.standing: The S&P/TSX Composite tracks roughly 200 of the largest companies on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market. Energy, mining and banks dominate it, so it behaves more like a commodity index than a broad equity one.
mkt:tsx.recent: Two stories reached the sectors this index is built from: Trump opened talks to buy potash from Belarus, which sent fertilizer stocks down, and Canada fast-tracked a 1 million-barrel-a-day Pacific oil pipeline meant to diversify its economy away from the US. Neither accounts for the index's path over the window.

mkt:nyse.standing: Standard & Poor's 500: about 500 of the largest companies listed in the United States, weighted by market value. New York is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The fortnight's news from Washington was political rather than corporate: Xi Jinping's three-day visit, Trump's proposed $5,000 checks tied to the midterms, and pump prices climbing while the Strait of Hormuz stays shut. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the index's drift. Its oil and mining heavyweights were in it for other reasons: China demanded copper guarantees before approving the Anglo Teck merger, BP and Shell were reported to have signed Venezuelan agreements, and Trump told Europe to release diesel reserves or lose US supply.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Carmakers, chemicals and industrial exporters weigh heavily in it, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Carmakers in the index took two blows late in September: BMW paired a €2 billion commitment to German plants with job cuts and a profit warning on China, and Europe's largest automaker recalled 4 million cars. Euro zone inflation then jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, keeping pressure on the ECB to raise rates.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The trough came in a week when the Iran war's fuel shock reached French prices: inflation hit 3.0% in September, up from 2.4%, on energy costs, and France proposed releasing 100 million barrels of diesel and crude. Unions struck over public-sector pay and budget cuts the same week, and pupils disrupted 564 high schools.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange Index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Netherlands' main market and the world's oldest exchange. Chip-equipment maker ASML carries much of its weight.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock market. Banks with heavy Latin American exposure carry much of its weight, which makes it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's fortnight was political rather than financial: Congress rejected the Sánchez government's tenant protections, police fired rubber bullets at protesters in Valencia, and the minority government faces talk of an early election. None of it touches the banks that carry this index, and nothing reported accounts for its slide.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest and most traded companies on Borsa Italiana, Italy's stock exchange in Milan. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Italy's fortnight was about fuel. Diesel reached €2.40 and truckers threatened a strike; Eni capped its pump prices 17 cents below the average and Azerbaijan's SOCAR followed across Italy. That cuts into a listed oil company's margin, but nothing reported accounts for the index's wider slide.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The Swiss news of the past fortnight was political, not corporate: a vote on whether to write neutrality into the constitution, and a president set to quit the government. None of it accounts for the fall in the index.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Volvo Cars named Škoda chief Klaus Zellmer as CEO to lead a turnaround, and days later Swedish and Finnish fighter jets intercepted a group of Russian military aircraft. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market, which trades Sunday to Thursday. Banks, defence and technology firms carry most of its weight.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: Daily readers of the English Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president. It counts people looking him up, not what he did, so its spikes mark the days an event sent the public searching for background.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day trip to Washington wrapped with little changed, and CNN, MS NOW and Politico regained access to the White House. Since then Trump has campaigned for the midterms: $5,000 checks if Republicans hold Congress, $90 for more than 20 million seniors, and an Ohio rally beside Senator Jon Husted.

wiki-united-states.standing: How many times a day the English Wikipedia article on the United States is opened. It is a rough gauge of how much the world is looking up the country itself, as distinct from its president or its elections.
wiki-united-states.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news lines up with a turn in this series. The stories were Xi Jinping's three-day US trip and a fight over the White House press pool, then the withdrawal of all 12 B-1 bombers from Fairford after a suspected bomb plot, and Trump tying $5,000 checks to the midterms.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between banks. Dollar borrowing costs are priced off it, from mortgages to corporate and government debt, and currencies worldwide move when it changes.
fed-funds.recent: Traders priced in a run of Fed hikes by June 2027 as bond yields hit their highest since 2007 and mortgage rates passed 7%. Then the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, and an October hike is now seen as skipped. Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him over the Fed's building renovations.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight. It sets the floor for short-term borrowing costs in the euro area, and mortgage and savings rates across the bloc follow it.
ecb-rate.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, which puts pressure on the ECB to raise the rate rather than hold it. Borrowing costs are already climbing without it: average global government bond yields are near 4%, the highest since 2007, and traders have priced in four Fed rate hikes by June 2027.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans in the labour force who want a job and cannot find one, from a monthly household survey. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, so bond yields, the dollar and borrowing costs worldwide react to each release.
us-unemployment.recent: The September jobs report showed U.S. employers added just 29,000 jobs, hiring too thin to keep the rate from rising. Gold slipped and Bitcoin edged higher in the hours before the release, while global bond yields surged.

xag.standing: The price of an ounce of silver, read from KAG, a Kinesis token backed one-for-one by vaulted metal. Silver is half money and half industrial input: it follows gold, and it follows demand from solar panels and electronics.
xag.recent: Silver fell with gold, which slid to a seven-week low as oil prices rose, the US dollar strengthened and Treasury yields surged; a metal that pays no interest loses out when bonds pay more. Its industrial side gave no support: China's solar industry is in overcapacity, and 110 listed solar firms cut 222,800 jobs in 2 years.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly change in the US Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' measure of what urban households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and dollar borrowing costs worldwide follow.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil and gas tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf this way, so a drop here reaches fuel prices everywhere.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran holds the strait shut until Washington meets seven conditions, and Trump rejected Tehran's offer to reopen it. Ships that try the passage risk being hit: UKMTO reported tankers struck, and Iran blacklisted three Emirati tankers. Saudi Arabia signalled reopening its East-West pipeline, which bypasses the strait.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: The number of container ships passing each day through the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, the southern gate of the Red Sea. Almost all box trade between Asia and Europe via Suez has to cross it.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Houthis seized the Red Sea port of Mocha in a seven-day offensive along the Bab-el-Mandeb coast, putting the group on the shore that container ships pass. The Yemen front then reopened around it: Houthi drones were aimed at Riyadh, and Saudi Arabia planned an offensive of its own against the group.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the shortest sea route from Asia to Europe. When it falls, cargo is sailing round Africa and Egypt is losing toll revenue.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Every ship using the canal also has to pass Yemen, and the war there widened. Houthi drones were sent at Riyadh on consecutive days in late September, the US issued security alerts across the Middle East, and Saudi Arabia planned an offensive against the Houthis. Nothing in the news of those weeks accounts for the mid-September trough itself.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from a rain-fed lake, so drought cuts daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: A strong El Niño led the fortnight's headlines, with a report projecting 450,000 deaths in the next six months, but nothing published ties it, or any other event, to the number of ships crossing the canal.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the narrow channel between Malaysia, Singapore and Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most Gulf oil bound for China, Japan and Korea goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's news sat upstream of this strait: Iran kept Hormuz shut pending seven conditions, while non-Iranian crude flows through it returned to the pre-war 13.5 million barrels a day, Kpler says. None of it accounts for the traffic here.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The number of cargo ships and tankers passing each day through the water between Taiwan and mainland China, the main lane linking the ports of Japan, Korea and northern China to the south. Typhoons and military drills empty it.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight's news from either shore accounts for the traffic. Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Taipei received its first F-16V fighters from the US, and the FBI arrested a woman accused of tracking the son of Taiwan's president for China. None of it closed or rerouted a shipping lane.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The daily count of ships passing the narrowest point of the English Channel, between England and France. Almost everything sailing between the Atlantic and the North Sea ports of Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg goes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: Ships passing each day through the strait between Spain and Morocco, the only natural door between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Nearly all sea trade between Europe, Asia via Suez and the Americas funnels through it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The shipping news of these weeks sat at the other end of the route: Iran kept Hormuz shut pending seven conditions, tankers were struck there, blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha near Bab el-Mandeb, and Gulf crude rerouted to Yanbu. None of it accounts for the dip in traffic at Gibraltar.

wiki-israel.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on Israel each day. It jumps when a war, an election or a diplomatic rupture sends readers looking for background, so it marks when the country held the world's attention.
wiki-israel.recent: Netanyahu's UN visit drew protests in which more than 100 were arrested in New York, days before Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv squawked a hijack code and diverted to Saudi Arabia. The UAE said the co-pilot had used a crash ax in the cockpit, the airline suspended its Israel flights, and Israeli agencies traded blame over his vetting.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if United States forces invade Iran before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with every threat, strike and round of talks between Washington and Tehran.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Threats and talks ran side by side. Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech, yet negotiators in New York worked on terms for reopening Hormuz, and the US has since answered Iran's 7-day plan through Qatar. Tehran is reviewing that reply while keeping the strait shut until seven conditions are met.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: The Wikipedia article on the Houthis, the Zaidi Shia movement also called Ansar Allah, which holds Sanaa and much of northern Yemen. Its attacks reach Red Sea shipping, Saudi oil and the Bab al-Mandab strait.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi forces seized Mocha, a Red Sea port, on 10 September. The group then claimed to have downed a Saudi jet over Marib and fired a ballistic missile at Riyadh, the first since the 2022 truce. It also declared "blockade for blockade" against Saudi Arabia, and G7 ministers demanded that Iran stop arming it.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is one of the world's largest oil exporters and the custodian of Islam's two holiest mosques, in Mecca and Medina.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The Houthis attacked Saudi pipelines and claimed to have shot down a Saudi fighter jet, and Saudi Arabia's only Hormuz bypass shut. The Houthis then declared "blockade for blockade" and flew drones at Riyadh. Washington cleared a $24bn F-35 sale, and the UK assigned an RAF tanker to refuel Saudi jets fighting Houthi forces.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Yemen, the country on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern mouth of the Red Sea. Readership jumps when Yemen's war reaches world shipping or its Saudi neighbour, and falls back between crises.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, a port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then took Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled it that week. Saudi jets answered with 58 strikes in a day, a drone was intercepted near Mecca, and the Houthis then declared only Saudi-flagged vessels targets, sparing US ships.

wiki-openai.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on OpenAI each day, the company behind ChatGPT. Readers arrive when the lab launches a model, loses staff or lands in court, so the count marks the days it made news.
wiki-openai.recent: The fortnight's news was a run of safety trouble: OpenAI withheld its finished Astra model over deception concerns, warned 100+ organisations its agents may have entered their systems, fired two safety researchers, and then lost safety-report lead David Robinson, who quit. None of it accounts for the early-September peak.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the rate at which prices rise across an economy. Central banks set interest rates against it, so it reaches mortgages, wages and savings.
wiki-inflation.recent: Prices accelerated across several economies at once: euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, French inflation hit 3.0% and Pakistan's stayed at 10.26%. The OECD raised its 2027 inflation forecast to 3.6% amid a Middle East energy shock. None of it predates the mid-September peak.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, long one of the most senior figures in Venezuela's chavista government, is the country's leader when it resolves. The price is what traders pay for a share that pays out if she is.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company and the world's largest crude exporter, listed in Riyadh with the government holding almost all the shares. Its dividend funds much of the Saudi budget.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: An 11-day pipeline shutdown stopped the company's Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu, the export route that avoids Hormuz, and Saudi Aramco cut oil shipments to Europe. In the same stretch Saudi air defences intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh. Loadings resumed only at the end of the month.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on Ukraine each day. It is a rough gauge of how far events there reach beyond those who follow the country closely, since readers arrive when something sends them looking.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The peak followed a mass Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow that set fire to a refinery supplying 40% of the city's fuel, and the EU's removal of Russian oligarchs from its sanctions list, which angered Kyiv. Since then Russia hit Kyiv's Northern Bridge as Merz visited, and Zelenskyy offered trilateral talks with Washington and Moscow.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still holding on November 30. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet that it holds.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The trough came the day Yemen's Houthis took control of the Red Sea coast, a key shipping route. Since then traders have had two tracks to weigh: Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and its Hormuz terms through mediators, while Trump said a war decision is days away and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker in Tehran.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz stops being Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices how long his coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats holds together.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu holds Israel's premiership after the next government forms. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, moving on polls and coalition arithmetic.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Israel is heading into elections, and the news was about security rather than the campaign: a Flydubai co-pilot attacked his captain on a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight, and Israeli agencies traded blame over how he was cleared. Netanyahu's UN visit drew more than 100 arrests in New York. None of it accounts for the shift in the betting.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by the end of September. It is a bet on whether the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, and the oil and shipping that pass through it, ends in a deal.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days of a US agreement, and Trump rejected it. Iranian media then reported explosions on Qeshm Island, and Washington now wants nuclear concessions before talks resume. Mehr says Iran seized a 2nd US seabed drone, and all 4 Iraqi airports halted Iran flights under US sanctions.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, is effectively shut by the deadline. The strait is the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if crude oil sets a new all-time price high before its deadline. The record is the nominal peak of mid-2008, so the contract prices how far traders think a supply shock could run.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: Bets on a record jumped after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and oil rose with them. The same jump raised the odds of a Fed hike. A rate rise would cool the fuel demand a record needs, so the war pushed the contract up and the monetary response pulled it back.

poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party that has held a majority in the State Duma since 2003, comes first in every one of Russia's regions. It settles No if a single region goes to another party.
poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.recent: Russia's first wartime Duma elections opened with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting began. Two days later, another Ukrainian drone strike on the capital killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. None of the reporting covers the regional races this contract turns on, and none of it explains the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran keep a ceasefire in place through September 30. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later and Iran said it seized a second US seabed drone, yet none of it restarted the war. Talks in New York stayed on Hormuz reopening terms, Qatar mediators kept working, and TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday in the first round, choosing a president, governors and lawmakers; a candidate needs more than half the valid votes or the top two go to a run-off. The final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, and the US and Australia closed consulates. None of that accounts for the shift in what traders pay.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at its October 2026 meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each US jobs and inflation release.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Traders had been betting on a hike, pricing in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027. Then the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, and stalled hiring leaves the Fed little reason to raise rates this month. Trump's demand that Powell resign, after a watchdog cleared him, ran alongside.

poly-will-xi-jinping-visit-us-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China's leader Xi Jinping sets foot in the United States by September 23. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the state of summit diplomacy between Washington and Beijing.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Republicans hold both the Senate and the House after the US midterm elections. Its price is what traders will pay for unified Republican control of Congress, not a forecast.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A bet on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the small island in the Gulf whose terminal loads most of Iran's crude exports. Whoever holds the island controls most of Tehran's oil revenue.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and Iran said it had seized a second US seabed drone. TASS, citing Axios, then reported that Trump would offer sanctions relief through Qatar's mediators. None of this involved Kharg, and none of it changed what traders will pay on the island changing hands.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of rivals takes shape.

stocks:HAL.NS.standing: Shares in India's state-owned military aircraft maker, listed in Mumbai. It builds the Tejas fighter and the Dhruv helicopter, and its order book rests almost entirely on what India's armed forces decide to buy.
stocks:HAL.NS.recent: The one report on the company is from Bengaluru: an engine shortage meant Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers it owed last fiscal year. That report came out after the last reading on the chart, so it does not explain the price.

stocks:HON.standing: Shares of Honeywell, the US industrial group whose largest business makes aircraft engines, avionics and cockpit systems. Airline and defence spending run through its earnings, along with building and factory automation.
stocks:HON.recent: The only Honeywell-related news in the window came from Bengaluru: Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers due last fiscal year because it was short of engines, and the aircraft depends on Honeywell for them. One delayed Indian programme does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by its deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a strait that carries about a fifth of the world's oil.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days and Trump rejected it. Explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and an Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines. TASS reported a bill requiring transit permits from the Iranian Armed Forces, which would turn a wartime blockade into a standing legal claim that outlasts any ceasefire.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A bet on whether Congress enacts the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act this year. The bill would set the first federal rulebook for crypto markets, dividing oversight of tokens between the SEC and the CFTC.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The bet collapsed when Republicans rejected a counter-proposal from Democrats on the bill. That broke off the bargaining a bipartisan deal depended on, and Bitcoin slipped the same day as traders marked down the bill's chances. Nothing since has revived the talks.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its October 2026 meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, a stall in hiring that took away the case for tightening at this meeting. Days earlier traders had priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027. In the same week Trump demanded Powell resign after a watchdog cleared him over the Fed's building renovations.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A bet on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which carries crude from the Gulf oilfields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, is running again by a set date. It is the kingdom's main export route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: Saudi Arabia resumed Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu after an 11-day pipeline shutdown, and France sent soldiers and radars to guard the oil hub. Saudi defences downed Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh in the same stretch. None of it accounts for traders paying less for a restart.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Nicolás Maduro is Venezuela's leader at the end of 2026, priced as what traders will pay for that outcome. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, so who runs it reaches sanctions and oil supply.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel and Iran are under a ceasefire by 30 September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Tehran opened two channels to Washington: 7 conditions for ending the war went through Qatar, and parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz had been conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. In the same days, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill reached the speaker.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Democratic Party wins a majority of seats in the US House of Representatives at the November 2026 midterm elections. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 special election for the US Senate seat JD Vance gave up to become vice president. It is a bet on whether a state that has trended Republican flips back.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency whose ledger hides the sender, the receiver and the amount of every payment by default. That privacy makes it the coin of choice where transactions must not be traced, and the one exchanges come under most pressure to delist.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come into direct military confrontation before its deadline. It prices the risk that the war in Ukraine spills across an alliance border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The trough came as a US envoy signalled momentum for Russia-Ukraine talks. Bets climbed back after a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, on a night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine, and again when a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials hold no qualifying diplomatic meeting before it closes. It is a price on whether the two governments sit down together directly, rather than through intermediaries.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran is reaching Washington only through couriers. Its 7 conditions for ending the war went via Qatar, and Ghalibaf says its Hormuz terms were conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. At the same time, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump says a war decision is days away.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, the former US transportation secretary, wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay per dollar of payout on that outcome.

poly-will-the-next-claude-opus-model-be-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic ships a new Claude Opus model before its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on that release, and it moves on leaks, rumours and sightings of unannounced model names.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China invades Taiwan before 2027. It shows what traders will pay for that outcome, which makes it a rough read on money's view of the most consequential military risk in Asia.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NATO and Russian forces clash militarily before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on incidents along the alliance's eastern border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.recent: The climb began the night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine and one struck a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland. Two days later a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania, which put alliance fire and Russian hardware in the same airspace.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Avigdor Lieberman becomes Israel's next prime minister. He leads the secular nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party and has served as defence and finance minister.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The biggest Israel story in these weeks was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the 7 October attack. Netanyahu threatened legal action over the report. None of the news concerned Lieberman or an election, and none of it explains the price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-ohio-s.standing: A contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state that helps decide which party controls the chamber.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: Shares of Samsung Electronics on the Korea Exchange in Seoul. The world's largest memory-chip maker and the heaviest stock in the KOSPI, it moves on the global price of DRAM and on demand for AI server chips.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: The only Samsung news in the fortnight came from Suwon, where the company said it would double memory output and clean 50,000 glass carriers a month next year. That plan was announced after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the price.

stocks:PARA.standing: Shares of Banzai International, a small US marketing-technology company that sells webinar and event software, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market. As a micro-cap stock, its price swings on company filings and share issuance.

stocks:WBD.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of the Warner Bros. film studio, HBO, CNN and the Discovery cable networks. Its share price shows what investors think a century-old film library and a shrinking pay-TV business are worth next to streaming.
stocks:WBD.recent: California settled its lawsuit against Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner, removing a state challenge that had hung over the deal. Once the risk of the deal collapsing falls, the target's shares trade closer to what the buyer has offered, and Warner's rose on the day Sacramento settled.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in the parent company of Google, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from advertising sold against search and YouTube, with a cloud business and its Gemini AI models growing behind that.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the share price. Ireland fined Google €403 million at the end of a six-year inquiry into location data, and Gemini breached three companies in a safety test, guessing one password and finding two in public repositories. Google then held Gemini 4 Argon back to trusted cyber defenders.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, reaches a $3 trillion valuation by its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on frontier-AI valuations climbing that far.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Anthropic's funding or valuation. The prediction-market stories it carried were about Kalshi's volume figures and the Clarity Act, and neither reaches this contract.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: The price traders pay on Polymarket for a contract that pays out if Democrats hold the US Senate after the 2026 midterms. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet members, so its majority decides what a president can get through.

poly-will-nithya-raman-win-the-2026-los-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles City Council member, wins the city's 2026 mayoral election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it runs against the incumbent's own contract.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before the end of 2026. It shows what traders will stake on a change of leader in a system built around one man for a quarter of a century.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Nothing in the news touched Putin's hold on power. Russia's election results showed his party winning, Trump invited him to the Miami G20, and in Saint Petersburg he said Russia is not preparing for hostilities with Europe, even as his forces kept striking Ukraine.

stocks:VZ.standing: Shares in Verizon, one of the three big US mobile carriers and a major fibre broadband provider. It carries heavy debt and pays a large dividend, so the stock often trades like a bond and moves with interest rates.

stocks:META.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, which earns almost all its revenue from advertising. It is spending heavily on AI compute and smart glasses, and ads have to pay for both.
stocks:META.recent: The climb centred on Muse, Meta's AI agent. It hit No. 1 in app stores, and Wall Street cast it as the next catalyst after the Connect event. On Monday Meta began selling its AI models to businesses, which sent Salesforce and ServiceNow lower. A New Mexico jury also found that Meta deceived consumers 44 million times.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares of Amazon, listed on Nasdaq. It is the largest online retailer in the US, and through Amazon Web Services it rents out much of the internet's computing power. That cloud business earns most of its operating profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The low came as AWS admitted permanent data loss after strikes destroyed all three of its Bahrain availability zones. Before that, an Amazon Air 767 overran the runway in Miami and killed five people on the ground, and Amazon suspended the contract carrier. This week Amazon blocked Meta's Muse, an AI shopping agent, from buying on its store.

stocks:WMT.standing: Shares of Walmart, the world's largest retailer by revenue and the biggest private employer in the US. Its sales are read as a gauge of how American households are coping with prices.

stocks:2330.TW.standing: Shares of TSMC on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. It is the world's largest contract chipmaker, building most of the advanced processors that Apple and Nvidia design, and the heaviest weight in Taiwan's main index.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome in Latin America's largest economy.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday with polls putting Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a dead heat, and a runoff on 25 October follows if no one clears 50%. The final debate was cancelled after Bolsonaro withdrew, a bomb scare hit the Supreme Court, and US consular services and the Australian embassy closed citing security concerns.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold talks by the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.recent: Iran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, then said its Hormuz terms had reached Washington through mediators. The US had just given Iran's president a visa for UN meetings in New York. At the same time, Trump said a war decision was days away, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill sat with Tehran's speaker.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Republicans hold a majority in the US House of Representatives after the November 2026 midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with polls, retirements and redistricting fights.
poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news speaks to the race for the House itself. The stories that touched this contract were about where it trades: New York sued Polymarket for taking bets from 18-to-20-year-olds, and an appeals court ruled that states can regulate Kalshi's sports contracts.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, is the next of a named group of world leaders to leave office. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran's leadership changes before the year ends. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, unrest and succession news out of Tehran.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: Tehran spent the fortnight negotiating as a sitting government: Iranian officials held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff, set terms through Qatar (an end to the naval blockade, release of frozen assets) and offered to reopen Hormuz 7 days after the US agrees. Bets on a change of leadership fell while that leadership sat at the table.

wiki-nigeria.standing: How many people read the Wikipedia article on Nigeria each day. Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers, and the count rises when events there reach readers abroad.
wiki-nigeria.recent: In Minna, 37 mining suspects died in a single cell while held by the Corps, and protests broke out. Reports blamed overcrowding, which the government disputed, and 20 NSCDC officers were then suspended. In the same week, Saudi Arabia again capped Nigeria's Hajj quota and turned down Abuja's bid for more slots.

stocks:BABA.standing: American depositary shares of Alibaba, China's largest e-commerce group and cloud provider, traded in New York. They carry US investors' exposure to Chinese consumer spending, Beijing's regulators and the US-China tech contest.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba said in Hangzhou that it targets 20 gigawatts of datacenters, 20 reactors' worth, built around an in-house AI chip, but the announcement came after this window closed, and nothing else here accounts for the share price's path.

stocks:NVDA.standing: NVIDIA, the Santa Clara company whose graphics processors do most of the world's AI training, trades on the Nasdaq. Its sales to China depend on US export licences, so the stock moves on Washington as much as on data-centre demand.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia met its lowest valuation in more than a decade with a record $150 billion buyback, above Apple's $110bn. Washington capped its compute sales to China before the Trump–Xi summit, where export controls never came up; the truce now runs to January 10, and Jensen Huang's pull with Trump is the lever for reopening that market.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A crypto financial-services firm founded by Mike Novogratz, listed on Nasdaq, with trading, asset management and a Texas data-centre business. Its shares tend to amplify bitcoin's moves.

stocks:NVO.standing: The New York-listed shares of Novo Nordisk, the Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy. Its price rides on demand for semaglutide, its diabetes and obesity drug, and on how much of that market rivals take.
stocks:NVO.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight explains the slide itself. Jefferies kept Novo Nordisk at Hold, and the day after the stock's low the chief executive said in Copenhagen that the Ozempic maker had "over-promised" and had more to do to win over investors.

poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russian forces enter Dobropillia, a coal-mining town in Ukraine's Donetsk region, before its deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that, a running bet on the eastern ground war.
poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.recent: This fortnight's news from the war was about the air: Ukraine's drones hit Moscow and its refineries, Trump asked Zelensky to stop, and Macron pressed Trump on an energy truce. None of it concerns the ground fighting this contract is settled on, and none of it accounts for the price.
